tagline: Over Utah's highest paved road, in a range that runs sideways.
intro: From Kamas, SR 150 winds east through farm and ranch land, then rises into heavily forested mountains broken by meadows and rugged peaks, with trailheads into the High Uintas Wilderness along the way. It crests at Bald Mountain Pass, 10,715 feet, the highest paved road in Utah, and then turns north to come down to the Wyoming line south of Evanston.
The Uintas are one of the few ranges in North America that run east to west. In winter the road is closed to cars and handed over to the snowmobiles.

moments.title: Kamas
moments.text: Named for the camas plant, the gateway town keeps the legend of a gold mine Ute guides showed Thomas Rhoads on condition he tell no one, and he never did.

moments.title: Mirror Lake
moments.text: The lake is named for its near-perfect reflection of the mountains and trees, seen from a roadside overlook, and the water leaving it becomes the Duchesne River.

moments.title: Hayden Peak
moments.text: Coming down from the pass the road goes by a peak named for the survey geologist Ferdinand Hayden, home to mountain goats and pika.

practical: The highway is closed to cars in winter and is typically open from mid-May to mid-fall. Driving it is free, but stopping at the recreation areas requires a Forest Service fee pass.
